body_header:
GRAPH INVARIANTS OF FINITE GROUPS VIA A




arXiv:math/0612618v1 [math.NT] 20 Dec 2006
                                                            THEOREM OF LAGARIAS

                                                                                 FÜSUN AKMAN


                                                     Abstract. We introduce a new graph invariant of finite groups that
                                                     provides a complete characterization of the splitting types of unramified
                                                     prime ideals in normal number field extensions entirely in terms of the
                                                     Galois group. In particular, each connected component corresponds to
                                                     a division (Abteilung) of the group. We compute the divisions of the
                                                     alternating group, and compile a list of characteristics of groups that the
                                                     invariant reveals. We conjecture that the invariant distinguishes finite
                                                     groups. Our exposition borrows elements from graph theory, group
                                                     theory, and algebraic number theory.




                                                                               1. Introduction
                                                In this article the term graph will mean, unless otherwise specified, a di-
                                             rected graph (digraph) where multiple directed edges (arcs) between adjacent
                                             vertices in the same direction and edges with one vertex (loops) are not al-
                                             lowed. The vertex and edge sets of the graphs will be colored and/or labeled.
                                             Our distinction between “color” and “label” is one of convenience; colors can
                                             be arbitrary objects whereas labels will be positive integers with certain addi-
                                             tive and multiplicative properties. All groups and graphs under consideration
                                             will be finite. The symbol An shall denote an alternating group and not a
                                             group of Lie type. We will not consider the problem of computational com-
                                             plexity.

body_header:
COVARIANT BIMODULE CONNECTIONS AND NONCOMMUTATIVE
                                                          GEOMETRIC YANG–BAXTER SOLUTIONS

                                                ALESSANDRO CAROTENUTO, ANTONIO DEL DONNO, RÉAMONN Ó BUACHALLA,
                                                                      AND JUNAID RAZZAQ




arXiv:2512.23579v2 [math.QA] 19 Oct 2026
                                                   Abstract. We introduce a new class of Yang–Baxter solutions, which we call non-
                                                   commutative geometric solutions, constructed from quantum group noncommutative
                                                   geometries. These solutions are built from a quantum homogeneous space, endowed
                                                   with a covariant differential graded algebra and a noncommutative Koszul connection
                                                   ∇. If ∇ is a bimodule connection, that is, if its generalised flip map σ is well defined,
                                                   then a simple set of sufficient conditions for σ to be a Yang–Baxter solution is given.
                                                   These results are applied to the cominuscule quantum flag manifolds Oq (G/LS ) en-
                                                   dowed with their Heckenberger–Kolb calculi. The noncommutative complex geometry
                                                   of the calculi decomposes their Yang–Baxter operator σ into three parts: holomorphic,
                                                   anti-holomorphic, and cross-type. For the non-exceptional examples, the holomorphic
                                                   and anti-holomorphic solutions recover, up to scalar multiple, the usual quasitriangular
                                                   braidings of the associated Drinfeld–Jimbo Uq (lsS )-modules. However, we get a new
                                                   extension of these braidings to the direct sum, which remarkably restricts to an invo-
                                                   lutive operator on the cross terms. As an application, we produce a simple uniform
                                                   presentation of the degree two relations of the Heckenberger–Kolb calculi as a quantum
                                                   exterior algebra associated to the generalised flip map σ.

body_header:
A Dolbeault complex for
                                                            the contact quantised flag manifolds
                                                                     of type C2 and D4
                                                                                      Antonio Del Donno∗1
                                                                    1
                                                                   Mathematical Institute of Charles University
                                                                Sokolovská 49/83, 18675 Prague 8, Czech Republic.




arXiv:2610.40076v1 [math.QA] 29 Oct 2026
                                                                                         October 30, 2026


                                                 Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the A-series have recently been
                                                 investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential
                                                 geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag
                                                 manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types C and D whose classical spaces
                                                 are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger–Kolb framework, we construct
                                                 covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact
                                                 directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type C2 , however, adjoining
                                                 the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal
                                                 prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-
                                                 dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical
                                                 dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those
                                                 of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type D4 , we show that adjoining
                                                 the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its
                                                 maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.

                                           Subject Classification: 58B32, 16T05, 20G42, 46L87.
                                           Keywords: noncommutative differential geometry, Hopf algebras, quantum groups.

                                                                      THOMAS M. RICHARDSON

                                                                   WESTERN MICHIGAN UNIVERSITY

                                                     Abstract. A Filbert matrix is a matrix whose (i, j) entry is 1/Fi+j−1 , where
                                                     Fn is the nth Fibonacci number. The inverse of the n × n Filbert matrix
                                                     resembles the inverse of the n × n Hilbert matrix, and we prove that it shares
                                                     the property of having integer entries. We prove that the matrix formed by
                                                     replacing the Fibonacci numbers with the Fibonacci polynomials has entries
                                                     which are integer polynomials. We also prove that certain Hankel matrices
                                                     of reciprocals of binomial coefficients have integer entries, and we conjecture
                                                     that the corresponding matrices based on Fibonomial coefficients have integer
                                                     entries. Our method is to give explicit formulae for the inverses.

EHRHART POLYNOMIALS OF
                                                      MATROID POLYTOPES AND POLYMATROIDS

                                                      JESÚS A. DE LOERA, DAVID C. HAWS, AND MATTHIAS KÖPPE


                                                   Abstract. We investigate properties of Ehrhart polynomials for matroid poly-




arXiv:0710.4346v1 [math.CO] 23 Oct 2007
                                                   topes, independence matroid polytopes, and polymatroids. In the first half of
                                                   the paper we prove that for fixed rank their Ehrhart polynomials are com-
                                                   putable in polynomial time. The proof relies on the geometry of these poly-
                                                   topes as well as a new refined analysis of the evaluation of Todd polynomials.
                                                   In the second half we discuss two conjectures about the h∗ -vector and the co-
                                                   efficients of Ehrhart polynomials of matroid polytopes; we provide theoretical
                                                   and computational evidence for their validity.




                                                                               1. Introduction
                                              Recall that a matroid M is a finite collection of subsets F of [n] = {1, 2, . . . , n}
                                          called independent sets, such that the following properties are satisfied: (1) ∅ ∈ F ,
                                          (2) if X ∈ F and Y ⊆ X then Y ∈ F , (3) if U, V ∈ F and |U | = |V | + 1 there
                                          exists x ∈ U \ V such that V ∪x ∈ F . In this paper we investigate convex polyhedra
                                          associated with matroids.
                                              One of the reasons matroids have become fundamental objects in pure and ap-
                                          plied combinatorics is their many equivalent axiomatizations. For instance, for a
                                          matroid M on n elements with independent sets F the rank function is a func-
                                          tion ϕ : 2[n] → Z where ϕ(A) := max{ |X| | X ⊆ A, X ∈ F }. Conversely a
                                          function ϕ : 2[n] → Z is the rank function of a matroid on [n] if and only if the
                                          following are satisfied: (1) 0 ≤ ϕ(X) ≤ |X|, (2) X ⊆ Y =⇒ ϕ(X) ≤ ϕ(Y ), (3)
                                          ϕ(X ∪ Y ) + ϕ(X ∩ Y ) ≤ ϕ(X) + ϕ(Y ). Similarly, recall that a matroid M can
                                          be defined by its bases, which are the inclusion-maximal independent sets. The
                                          bases of a matroid M can be recovered by its rank function ϕ. For the reader we
                                          recommend [31] or [40] for excellent introductions to the theory of matroids.

                                                   tangent spaces for the full quantum flag manifold Oq (Fn+1 ). The associated differential
                                                   calculi are direct q-deformations of the anti-holomorphic Dolbeault complex of the
                                                   classical full flag manifold Fn+1 . As an application we establish a quantum Borel–Weil
                                                   theorem for Oq (Fn+1 ), giving a noncommutative differential geometric realisation of
                                                   all the finite-dimensional type-1 irreducible representations of Uq (sln+1 ). Restricting
                                                   this differential calculus to the quantum Grassmannians is shown to reproduce the
                                                   celebrated Heckenberger–Kolb anti-holomorphic Dolbeault complex. Lusztig’s positive
                                                   root vectors for non-nice decompositions of the longest element of Sn+1 are examined
                                                   for low orders, and are exhibited to either not give tangents spaces, or to produce
                                                   differential calculi of non-classical dimension.

Bounds of some real (complex) solution of a ﬁnite system
                                                          of polynomial equations with rational coeﬃcients
                                                                         Apoloniusz Tyszka
                                              Abstract. We discuss two conjectures. (I) For each x1 , . . . , xn ∈ R (C) there exist




arXiv:math/0702558v86 [math.AC] 4 Dec 2009
                                              y1 , . . . , yn ∈ R (C) such that
                                                                                                                  n−2
                                                                                  ∀i ∈ {1, . . . , n} |yi| ≤ 22
                                                                            ∀i ∈ {1, . . . , n} (xi = 1 ⇒ yi = 1)
                                                                  ∀i, j, k ∈ {1, . . . , n} (xi + xj = xk ⇒ yi + yj = yk )
                                                                   ∀i, j, k ∈ {1, . . . , n} (xi · xj = xk ⇒ yi · yj = yk )
                                              (II) Let G be an additive subgroup of C. Then for each x1 , . . . , xn ∈ G there exist
                                              y1 , . . . , yn ∈ G ∩ Q such that
                                                                                  ∀i ∈ {1, . . . , n} |yi| ≤ 2n−1
                                                                            ∀i ∈ {1, . . . , n} (xi = 1 ⇒ yi = 1)
                                                                  ∀i, j, k ∈ {1, . . . , n} (xi + xj = xk ⇒ yi + yj = yk )

                                                 For a positive integer n we deﬁne the set of equations En by
                                                                              En = {xi = 1 : 1 ≤ i ≤ n} ∪
                                             {xi + xj = xk : 1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ n, 1 ≤ k ≤ n} ∪ {xi · xj = xk : 1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ n, 1 ≤ k ≤ n}
                                              Since there is a ﬁnite number of non-empty subsets of En , we get:

                                               (1) There is a function χ : {1, 2, 3, . . .} → {1, 2, 3, . . .} with the property: for each
                                                    positive integer n, if a non-empty subset of En forms a system of equations that
                                                    is consistent over Z, then this system has a solution being a sequence of integers
                                                    whose absolute values are not greater than χ(n).

                                               (2) There is a function γ : {1, 2, 3, . . .} → {1, 2, 3, . . .} with the property: for each
                                                    positive integer n, if a non-empty subset of En forms a system of equations that
                                                    is consistent over R, then this system has a solution being a sequence of real
                                                    numbers whose absolute values are not greater than γ(n).

                                               (3) There is a function θ : {1, 2, 3, . . .} → {1, 2, 3, . . .} with the property: for each
                                                    positive integer n, if a non-empty subset of En forms a system of equations that
                                                    is consistent over C, then this system has a solution being a sequence of complex
                                                    numbers whose absolute values are not greater than θ(n).
                                                   2000 Mathematics Subject Classification: 03B30, 12D99, 12L12, 14P05, 15A06, 26C10.
                                              Key words and phrases: system of polynomial (linear) equations, solution with minimal l∞ norm.
